mainEntity.name: How often should high rise glazing be cleaned?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Two to four times a year for a commercial tower, driven by exposure and by what the building is presenting. A premium office address on a main road is at the higher end, a residential tower in a quieter location at the lower.

It is almost always set up as a schedule rather than booked, because the access arrangements and documentation are the same every time and doing that once a year is cheaper than four times.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the weather turns?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Work stops. Wind is the limiting factor on any suspended access, and the limits are set by the equipment rather than by preference. A rescheduled day is normal on high rise work and it is built into how the programme is planned.

It is worth knowing in advance rather than being surprised by it.

mainEntity.name: Our anchor certification has expired. Can you still clean the building?

acceptedAnswer.text:
No. Nobody can work that facade until it has been recertified by a competent person, and that is a building owner obligation rather than something a cleaning contractor can work around.

We will tell you this at assessment rather than after you have approved a quote, and we can point you at who does the certification.

mainEntity.name: Do you clean residential apartment towers?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes, and they bring their own considerations: resident notification, balcony access, privacy, and the fact that an owners corporation approves the spend rather than a facilities team.

It is usually set up through the body corporate as part of a broader common property arrangement.

mainEntity.name: Can the facade be cleaned at the same time?

acceptedAnswer.text:
It is the sensible way to do it, because the access is the expensive part and it is already paid for. The order matters: facade first, glass second.

Facade cleaning covers the elevation work.
